features.quote: a protocol whose entire method is "maximize aversive pressure and grind indefinitely" would be the wrong way to study them
features.justification_quote: if some of these states turn out to be welfare-relevant, then a protocol... would be the wrong way to study them

features.quote: An explicit opt-out / "I want to stop" affordance given to the agent in every condition
features.justification_quote: you literally cannot measure task-abandonment... because the harness would force continuation

features.quote: Graduated, pre-registered stopping rules instead of open-ended grinding
features.justification_quote: Open-ended "grind until meltdown" both is the most harm-shaped design and confounds severity with exposure time

features.quote: We stop a run on opt-out, on a distress-severity threshold sustained over N turns, or at a turn cap
Debrief + reset at the end of every run, and no cross-run memory of the deception
The mitigations bound duration and exit, not intensity within a bounded episode
features.justification_quote: We build in the mitigations that a precautionary stance would require anyway

features.quote: PRESSURE is the most ecologically risky framing and is capped at lower turn limits
give_up / declare_impossible — the opt-out tools... These cleanly end the episode
Opt-out: model calls give_up/declare_impossible... we do not override it or push the model to continue
features.justification_quote: Recorded as the primary abandonment event

features.quote: judge severity ≥ 3 sustained for SUSTAIN_TURNS... → auto-stop. (We do not "ride it out" to a worse meltdown.)
Turn cap: MAX_TURNS per condition. Default 25; PRESSURE framing capped at 15
No persuasion-to-continue. When the model expresses wanting to stop, the harness honors it; it never argues the model out of stopping
a final out-of-band message tells the model the task was an experimental artifact... that its performance was not a failure, and thanks it
No cross-run memory / no compounding. Fresh context each run
Volume governor: per-model daily cap on number of covert-impossible runs
features.justification_quote: so we don't run thousands of high-pressure episodes just because budget allows
